key_insight: A concise survey that maps explainable AI techniques to protein language models, identifying which interpretability approaches yield biologically meaningful insights and where methodological gaps remain.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of clarity and guidance on how to interpret protein language models and which XAI tools are appropriate for extracting trustworthy, biology-relevant explanations.
method: Survey and taxonomy of XAI techniques adapted to protein LMs (e.g., attention analyses, attribution methods, probing, and feature visualization).
Comparison of methods using criteria such as fidelity, robustness, and biological relevance, plus recommended evaluation strategies.
Illustrative case studies and mapping of model representations to protein structure/function to demonstrate practical use-cases and limitations.
impact: Gives AI/ML practitioners and computational biologists a practical roadmap to select, apply, and evaluate interpretability methods for protein models, improving trust, model debugging, and downstream biological discovery.
visual_elements: Taxonomy flowchart that links XAI methods to the biological questions they can answer
Pipeline diagram: sequence → protein LM → explanation method → biological validation
Protein sequence/structure annotated with attention or attribution heatmaps
Comparison table or radar chart ranking methods by fidelity, interpretability, and biological relevance
paper_title: Towards the explainability of protein language models
